# ADDENDUM 26 — July 30, 2026 — THE WAIT SAGA (THE WIRE OUTRANKS THE LIBRARY, BOTH DIRECTIONS), THE STALENESS CASCADE ENDED, THE OPERATOR CATCHES THE LOOP BUG, THE UI TRUTH AUDIT, PALLET FRAME TEACHING SHIPS, AND SAMENESS LANDS
*(Appended in full. Nothing above this line was removed. One brutal, productive day: the first run of the motion integration collided with a wait-verb regression of our own making and a deployment pipeline that stalled four separate ways — ending with the execute-to-the-wire discipline, a completed run, the operator personally catching a loop-unaware classifier bug, a systematic UI truthfulness audit, the 3-point pallet orientation teaching shipped and then upgraded to the operator's 3-corners-plus-first-part spec, machine-tending vocabulary designed, free-drag revived as an ECO possibility, and the sameness feature landing against the real 63-step demonstration.)*

### Section 435: The staleness that started the day — services 25 hours behind the code

Morning finding, via the two-timestamp check: `roboai-dashboard`/`roboai-estun` started **July 28 13:42/13:54**; `program_ops.py` written **July 29 14:45** (sha `48ff6c60…` confirmed on disk). The entire motion integration had never loaded — every "joint move on the approach" observed since was the *old* codegen running faithfully. §408's exact shape, third instance, caught by §408's own check. Operator restarted both services; driver latched textbook (grace → READY → 7-topic burst; `operator_speed_limit=100%` live in the banner for the first time). Side note filed: an `env-zone fetch failed` warning at boot = a startup race (driver asked before the dashboard finished restarting; retries every 30s, self-heals, moot with zones deliberately empty).

### Section 436: The wait saga — error 10006, the drift, and the root cause we authored

First run of the integrated program: **10006 "invalid parameter" at line 11** — the `waitCondition(false,500)` emission, the integration's one flagged assumption, rejected on the wire. The fix directive produced a systemTime-loop replacement… and the next run failed at **line 12** — which the operator correctly read as *the same program position* (line numbers drift when code above changes; the position is the invariant). The NO-THIRD-GUESS directive (drop the wait entirely) was issued — and Claude Code, it turned out, **declined it on its own reasoning**, while a full status check revealed the day's true condition: **nothing had deployed at all** — zero commits, no restart after the sweep's edits, the resident Lua still carrying the *original* `waitCondition` line, and the frontend System Check showing a **false green** ("Up to date" computed from absence of data). Every fix had died in a working tree while the robot re-read the same broken line.

Then the operator asked the question that solved the day: *"why would it stop now when yesterday this program ran perfectly?"* — **because yesterday's program used `wait(500)`, and it ran clean.** Bare `wait()` is **wire-proven working** on firmware v2.3 despite being absent from `luaenginelib.json`. The integration's library audit had "fixed" a working line into documented-but-rejected alternatives. The regression was ours, authored from documentation against wire evidence.

### Section 437: Execute to the wire — the deploy that finally traveled

The corrective directive carried the deploy *inside* it: restore `wait(<ms>)` (whitelisted in the linter as WIRE-PROVEN/UNDOCUMENTED, evidence cited), record both rejected idioms in the verb reference, **commit → build → restart → re-push → read the controller's own copy back**. Executed in full: served asset hash changed (Bv_GRHDP → C6wP9edg), boot-sha = disk-sha = resident-sha (first three-way agreement of the day), resident line 11 = `wait(500)` with the lint footer, and the System Check's false green replaced with an honest amber "cannot verify" when it lacks a comparison basis. **The run that followed completed** — cursor watched crossing line 10's `setDO(2,1)` and past the wait that had killed every prior attempt. First completed run of the fully integrated motion stack.

### Section 438: Reading the run — the motion truths in the Lua

The executing program's own annotations mapped the operator's observations precisely: line 7's movJ transit carried `orient_dev max=8.99° (!)` (the taught-pose inconsistency, boom-amplified); line 9's movL descend stamped `wrist_dev=max0.00°` (the column fix, running); line 13 printed the analyzer's verdict `awkward_wrist_transit: wrist delta 55.2° — forcing joint-space transit`. The "extra joint move up and down to pick" was identified as **the loop-return transit**: each cycle ends at place (J1=+7.4°, J6=−165.8°) and returns to above-pick (J1=+62.6°, J6=−110.6°) — 55° of base and wrist expressed as the movJ arc. Two fixes tabled: Straight transit (with the honest clearance tradeoff — the arc is accidental obstacle clearance) and the **place wrist re-teach** (kills the spin in every profile; the standing recommendation).

### Section 439: The columns-always-cartesian invariant runs — and the label lie dies

Operator: approach moves are joint while the program *says* linear. Two-part response shipped: (1) **label honesty** — step rows and Lua comments must state the emitted verb whenever it diverges from the step type ("move_linear · runs as joint — wrist Δ55°"), never bare divergence; (2) the **queued invariant executed**: approach *arrivals* emit movL in every profile (the column grows upward; profiles govern transits only), with the analyzer exception preserved (arrival wrist delta >30° → movJ with the printed reason). The per-segment report: **approach-above-pick flips to movL** (home/pick wrists agree, Δ0°); **approach-above-place stays movJ** — and the unlock quantified: re-teach place with **J6 ∈ [−140.6°, −80.6°]** and it flips automatically. A restart-skip nearly repeated the morning (run executed before the restart — caught by the served-bundle stamp), answered with the **deploy-staleness banner directive**: amber "code updated on disk — restart required" on the Program page + `scripts/deploy.sh` as the one atomic deploy command + `codegen_stale` surfaced in the run-complete toast.

### Section 440: The operator catches the loop bug — classifier was loop-unaware

Post-invariant observation, operator's own catch: **place→pick looked linear (it shouldn't)** — the classifier judged step 2's arrival by its *first-iteration* predecessor (home, Δ0° → movL) — but inside the `for` loop, **cycles 2–5 arrive from the place retreat (Δ55°)**: a straight line executed *with a spinning wrist* on every looped return, the exact motion rule 2e exists to forbid. Root cause: every "previous step" rule analyzed iteration 1 and stamped all N. Fix directive: **loop-aware predecessors** — any step in a loop body has two arrival contexts (pre-loop entry + loop-back from the body's last motion), and the emitted verb must satisfy the wrist rule and feasibility for BOTH (else movJ with the failing context named); applied to all previous-step rules (arrival detection, awkward-wrist, blend adjacency, short-segment). Conservative single-verb v1; per-context emission optional later. The accountability moment recorded alongside: after "will this actually work" × today, the standing answer changed — *no more forecasts; the re-teach is arithmetic; the robot gets the last word.*

### Section 441: The UI truthfulness audit — twelve findings, the fork disease named

Operator: "cross check everything — I can't keep finding these one at a time." The audit was designed around the day's three failure patterns: **duplicate resolvers** (frontend re-deriving what the backend already resolves), **labels that can diverge from reality** (computed from step-type/cache/absence rather than the authoritative value), and **controls that don't exist or don't act**. It ran — the report-only demo-day amendment did not land in time — and found **12 issues, fixing the LIES-severity set**: `doneCount` forked three ways (one fork reading a field nothing writes — always zero), the step-highlight map wrong for every program containing adaptation comments (now honestly absent rather than wrong), a shared `programTruth.js` resolver established, **15 new frontend tests**, and the **`no-fork-truth` lint guard** — new components physically cannot re-derive taught-state without failing CI. Deploy-day verdict: verify, don't revert — the changes were display-truth improvements; smoke-test protocol issued (hard refresh → demo path walk → one rehearsal cycle → freeze). Related single-instance fix queued: the edit-panel's "Source pose isn't taught yet" on a taught pose — the panel's preview resolver predates the §397 merge (the same fork disease; routes through the shared resolver).

### Section 442: Demo-day protocol + the robust-capture doctrine

Investor meeting held on the standing build under the freeze rule (rehearse twice at demo speed → freeze → nothing changes until after). The pre-flight check pattern recorded (read-only: services healthy, codegen_stale=False, resident lint footer, served hash, recorder headroom). Alongside, the operator's step-back question got the doctrine on record — **what a correct program requires**: the six-item action taxonomy (motion ×4 / I/O / waits / flow / modal settings / machine coordination) and the **five kinds of capture** — poses (taught *joints*, consistency enforced at teach time), per-segment intent (surviving to the emitted verb through every context — the loop lesson), explicit structure (linking/derivation/repetition), physical context (payload/tool/cell — "the controller believed the flange was bare for three months"), and **the verification loop** (resident read-back, trajectory measurement, codegen stamps): *captured intent must be checkable against what actually runs.*

Twin ghost-slot rendering deferred (endpoint complete, viewer consumption pending). Then two follow-ups: **legacy migration** (frame points added on open; Edit-panel per-point Teach buttons; the pallet step's DO1/DO0 gripper defaults routed through the effector module) and the **v2 spec from the operator**: **three actual CORNERS** ([1,1], [1,N], [M,1] — instructions a human understands, pitches measured for free) **plus a separate ④ first-part position** (frame vs part-datum separation — the corner is fixture geometry; the part pose is contact truth), with the diagram rendering **live in the teach drawer** per point. ### Section 445: The deploy script's own staleness bug

Operator: "where is the teach for the pallet? It's missing." Footer showed served bundle `B7rsy59W` while the pallet-frame deploy's log had printed *"served bundle up to date; **skipping build**"* — **the build-check had a false negative** (ProgramWizard.jsx was modified; the heuristic said otherwise). The deploy script built to end staleness had a staleness bug. Fix directive: build-needed decided by **source state** (git diff / content hash of frontend/src since last build), never mtime/bundle-presence heuristics — *when in doubt, build*; plus the acceptance test stated as one number the operator can read: **Teach All (6)** on the test program (home, pick, home-return + pallet A/B/C).

### Section 446: Free drag revived — the ECO hypothesis and the bench procedure

Full-manual review of the drag question, with a record correction: §119's decision was **Pro** (torque sensors, smooth drag); the delivered arm is the **ECO-V2** (`ExistTorqueSensor → false`, July 20). But the July 20 verdict "drag unavailable" was **too strong**: the hardware manual's monthly safety test instructs pressing the free-drive button on every S-series; the flange button "defaults to free drag" (HW §5.1.1); and the config sweep found drag fully parameterized (dragThresholdCoeff Medium, Drag Sensitivity 50). Reconciliation: **ECO drag = motor-current estimation** — functional, resistive-and-rough rather than torque-sensor smooth. **The historical blocker: payload 0 kg until July 29** — gravity compensation had nothing to compensate with. All documented preconditions now plausibly satisfied. Bench procedure issued: Parameter Identification first (controller *measures* mass/CoG — drag quality ∝ payload accuracy on current-based systems) → DI Function Configuration check + photo (button = Start/Stop Dragging, DI18–21) → Manual/enabled/Real-Machine/mid-workspace → press with a hand under it (acceptance per the manual: holds position unsupported) → error-code ladder (16005/6 init, 16009 pose, 16012 sim mode). Payoff if it works: every teach — positions, pallet corners, waypoints — becomes grab-place-record.

### Section 447: The descent question sent to the evidence — and the three-layer label answer

Operator: physical joint moves down to pick AND place while the program says linear. Response: **no theories — the diagnose-from-evidence directive**: (1) resident Lua verbatim for both columns (which verb is on the wire), (2) run provenance (codegen stamp, stale flag), (3) **trajectory numbers** — TCP line deviation (mm) and orientation deviation (deg) per descent, (4) the verdict table — movJ-on-wire = classifier defect (print the rule); movL + ~0 deviation = **the motion IS linear** (joints visibly reconfiguring while the tool tracks a straight line is legal movL physics — the millimeters decide, not adjectives); movL + real deviation = a severe firmware finding, capture everything; (5) the label audit (is the divergence annotation rendering, and in which bundle). The "why does it say linear" question answered as doctrine: **the step type is what you asked for; the verb is what the robot gets; the screen's job is to show both whenever they differ.**

### Section 448: The 63-step discovery — and sameness lands against it

Program Library showed two programs named "white bowl Pick & Place": the wizard's 12-step (one cycle + loop) and a **63-step PBD-born** program — the composer had transcribed five demonstrated repetitions flat (no sameness, no condensation; both features designed, neither yet run). Operator: "let's run this so it can be smarter next time." **Sameness (§429) resumed and completed**: claimed-done tasks verified first (the rate-limit-cut lesson), composer one-ref-one-position dedup, review 🔗N badges with the no-questions contract (low-confidence renders as a passive chip), pinned tests (same-spot → 1 position N refs; distinct stays distinct; explicit speech overrides video) — and the acceptance run against the **real 63-step demo: resolved to one pick ref + one place ref + home.** Deployed, served hash verified. **Routines (§430) directive pasted next** — stacks on the location_ref keys; acceptance = the same 63-step program folding to ~one cycle ×5 with byte-identical emitted Lua (representation-only, zero wire change); includes the name-collision cleanup (rename the PBD program). The before/after pair designated demo material: *"the AI now understands that five repetitions are one task."*

## PROCESS LESSONS (157–164)

157. **The wire outranks the library — in both directions.** `wait()` is undocumented and works; `waitCondition(false,N)` is documented and rejected. Yesterday's clean runs were evidence, and we overrode evidence with documentation. Runtime-proven beats library-absent; library-listed guarantees nothing.
158. **Line numbers drift; program position is the invariant.** The operator's "it quit at the same spot" outdiagnosed the line-number comparison — the same failing instruction wore line 11 and line 12 in successive builds. Track failures by what the line IS, not where it sits.
159. **Execute to the wire, or it didn't happen.** Four fixes in one day died in working trees, unrestarted services, and skipped builds — while a false-green System Check vouched for all of them. A directive now carries its deploy inside it, and "done" means the controller's own copy read back correct.
160. **Loop bodies have two predecessors.** Every previous-step rule that analyzed iteration 1 stamped all N — the operator caught a straight-line-with-spinning-wrist on looped returns that the classifier structurally could not see. Any rule reading "the previous step" must evaluate both the entry edge and the loop-back edge.
161. **Deploy tooling gets the same skepticism as everything else.** The script built to end staleness skipped a build on a false heuristic its own log recorded. Build-needed is a source-state question; when in doubt, build — 60 seconds of redundancy against an afternoon of ghost-chasing.
162. **One surface per capability.** Teaching in a config modal, step names forked in a wizard, taught-state derived three ways — every duplicate surface eventually disagrees with the real one. Parameters in modals, teaching in the teach flow, one vocabulary module, one resolver — enforced by lint, not memory.
163. **The step type is intent; the verb is command; the screen shows both when they diverge.** "Says linear, runs joint" is legitimate exactly once — when the row says so and names the reason. Divergence is a design feature; silent divergence is a lie.
164. **Adjectives don't measure motion — millimeters do.** "It's making joint moves" and "the TCP tracked the line at 0.3mm deviation" can both be true: joints visibly reconfigure under a straight tool. When eyes and labels disagree, the trajectory table is the referee — in either direction.

---

*Summary of Addendum 26: the day the integration met the wire and everyone learned who outranks whom. The first run died on the one line the integration had guessed at — and the operator's "it ran perfectly yesterday" cracked the case: bare wait() was wire-proven all along, the library audit had regressed a working line, and every repair since had stalled in working trees and skipped restarts while a false-green health check vouched for the wreckage. The answer became doctrine — execute to the wire, deploy inside the directive, read the controller's copy back — and the run that followed completed, its own annotations narrating the motion truths: straight columns, designed transits, and a 55° wrist delta whose re-teach window is printed to the degree and still, eight days on, waiting for two minutes at the tablet. The operator out-diagnosed the tooling twice — same-spot-different-line, and the loop-unaware classifier stamping iteration 1's verb on all five cycles — and the day answered with loop-aware arrival contexts, a twelve-finding UI truthfulness audit that established the shared resolver and a lint guard against forked truth, and an afternoon batch that fixed unclearable numeric fields, the wizard's forked effector vocabulary, and the config modal that thought it was a teach pendant. Pallet teaching shipped its 3-point oriented frame with the diagram-guided flow, was immediately upgraded to the operator's better spec — three real corners plus a separate first-part datum, diagram live in the jog drawer — and exposed the deploy script's own staleness bug on the way. Free drag came back from the dead as an ECO current-based possibility now that the controller finally knows what it's carrying. And the flywheel turned visibly: sameness landed against the real 63-step demonstration and resolved it to one pick, one place, and home — with routines queued to fold the rest. Eight lessons, one completed run, and the standing sentence that ended the forecasting era: the robot gets the last word.*
